title: Build and manage Connected Apps in one place
gist: Google launched a preview of its Connected Apps Platform, letting developers build once via a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP (AppFunctions APIs) and distribute agentic app integrations into both Search and the Gemini app. Google says more than 50 Connected Apps are live, with partners such as Adobe, Experian, Localiza, Peloton and Calm, and access is opening in phases.

insights.claim: Google's new Connected Apps Platform requires developers to integrate through either a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, making the Model Context Protocol the standard plumbing for third-party apps in Search and the Gemini app.
insights.speaker: Chips Mistry
insights.so_what: Google's endorsement cements MCP as the cross-vendor standard for agent-to-app integration, lowering switching costs for developers across assistants.
insights.quote: Developers integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app.

insights.claim: Google's Connected Apps Platform is pitched as 'build once' distribution to high-intent users across both Search and the Gemini app, unifying what were separate integration surfaces.
insights.speaker: Chips Mistry
insights.so_what: Search's commercial-intent traffic becomes an agent-action channel, a potential new monetization surface beyond ads.
insights.quote: The Connected Apps Platform gives developers the opportunity to build once and reach high-intent users across both Search and the Gemini app.

insights.claim: Developers on Google's Connected Apps Platform register, test and submit apps through a new Google Connected Console and choose before review whether the app goes live in Search, the Gemini app, or both, implying a Google-run review gate akin to an app store.
insights.speaker: Chips Mistry
insights.so_what: Google retains gatekeeper control over which brands get agentic distribution, a lever for future platform economics.
insights.quote: Before review, developers choose whether it will go live in Search, the Gemini app, or both.

insights.claim: Once a Connected App is live, Google gives developers dashboards for traffic, latency and error rates plus control of brand identity via verified logos and authenticated accounts.
insights.speaker: Chips Mistry
insights.so_what: Brand-control and analytics features address the main merchant fear of disintermediation by AI assistants, easing partner adoption.
insights.quote: Once live, you can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and keep control of your brand identity, including verified logos and authenticated accounts.

insights.claim: Google's Connected Apps Platform launched only as a preview with phased access, with more developers, markets and Google products to be added over the coming months.
insights.speaker: Chips Mistry
insights.so_what: Expansion to other Google products suggests the MCP-based app layer may extend beyond Search and Gemini, broadening its reach over time.
insights.quote: We're opening access in phases, and will add more developers, markets, and Google products over the coming months.

insights.claim: Google has launched more than 50 Connected Apps across Search and Gemini, spanning productivity, event ticketing, and health and fitness.
insights.speaker: Chips Mistry
insights.so_what: A 50+ app catalog is an early but meaningful baseline for tracking Gemini's agentic ecosystem against rival assistant app stores.

insights.claim: Connected App integrations from Adobe, Experian, Localiza and Peloton are live in Gemini and will come to Search in the coming weeks, with a new Calm integration launching across both.
insights.speaker: Chips Mistry
insights.so_what: Named consumer brands, including a credit bureau (Experian), signal willingness to expose services, even in financial data, inside Google's AI surfaces.
insights.quote: Integrations with partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, and Peloton are live for users in Gemini, and in the coming weeks, we’ll be bringing these Connected Apps to Search as well.

insights.claim: The sequencing of Connected Apps going live in Gemini first and reaching Search weeks later implies Google uses the Gemini app as the proving ground before exposing agentic integrations to its far larger Search audience.
insights.speaker: Chips Mistry
insights.so_what: Watch the Search rollout as the moment agentic actions reach mass scale and start affecting referral traffic to partner sites.
